subject: Human Body
title: Capillaries
description: A fast breakdown of Capillaries for builders.

hook.text: Capillaries are so thin that red blood cells pass through one at a time. This is where the real work happens.

buildup.text: Their walls are one cell thick. Oxygen, nutrients, and waste pass through by diffusion in fractions of a second.

discovery.text: Laid end to end, your capillaries would stretch over 60,000 miles. Every cell in your body sits near one.

twist.text: Not all capillaries are open at once. The body opens and closes them based on local demand, directing flow where needed.

climax.text: Arteries deliver. Veins return. But capillaries are the exchange counters. Without them, blood flow is meaningless.

punchline.text: 60,000 miles of tubes one cell thin. That's the real network.
